title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: 𝔖 is (a copy of) GL(2,Z), with 𝔖^+ = SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. Its elements are ρ (order 6), σ (order 4) with σ^2 = ρ^3 = -1, τ' a reflection of determinant -1, and τ = στ'. A finite (or profinite) quotient 𝔊^+ of SL(2,Z) comes with an 'extended automorphism group' G_{ρ,σ} ⊃ 𝔊^+ carrying characters χ_G, ε_G, ε'_G. 𝔖 has been embedded into G_{ρ,σ}. L_ρ = ⟨ρ⟩ and L_σ = ⟨σ⟩ are the cyclic subgroups. Z_ρ and Z_σ are the centralizers of ρ and σ in G_{ρ,σ}.

This page does the following:
(34) Since τ' normalizes L_ρ and L_σ (it inverts ρ and σ), it acts on Z_ρ and Z_σ. Grothendieck forms the external semidirect products N_ρ = {1,τ'} ⋉ Z_ρ and N_σ = {1,τ'} ⋉ Z_σ.
(35) These give split exact sequences 1 → Z → N → {±1} → 1.
(36)–(37) There is a commutative diagram of canonical maps. The Klein four-group {1,τ'}×{±1} = D_ρ ∩ D_σ sits in D_ρ ≅ D_6 = ⟨ρ,τ'⟩ (order 12) and in D_σ ≅ D_4 = ⟨σ,τ'⟩ (order 8), both inside GL(2,Z). These map to N_ρ and N_σ and then, via i_ρ and i_σ, into G_{ρ,σ}. This is the image in G of the classical amalgam GL(2,Z) = D_4 *_{D_2} D_6.
(38) D_ρ = {1,τ'}·L_ρ as soon as ρ has order 6 in G, and similarly D_σ = {1,τ'}·L_σ when σ has order 4. Then D_ρ → N_ρ and D_σ → N_σ are injective. The page also asserts that i_ρ and i_σ are injective, but (39) qualifies this.
(39) The precise criterion: i_ρ is injective ⇔ τ' ∉ Z_ρ ⇔ ρ^2 ≠ 1. The reason is that τ'ρτ' = ρ^{-1}, so τ' centralizes ρ iff ρ^2 = 1. Under the standing assumption ρ ≠ 1, this is equivalent to ρ ≠ -1. In the degenerate case ρ^2 = 1, we get ρ = ρ^3 = σ^2. Then 𝔊^+ = ⟨ρ,σ⟩ is generated by σ alone, hence is a quotient of Z/4Z. The same criterion holds for σ: i_σ is injective ⇔ τ' ∉ Z_σ ⇔ σ^2 ≠ 1.

Purpose: the next page shows that i_ρ(N_ρ) and i_σ(N_σ) are the normalizers in G of L_ρ and L_σ. It defines the subgroups N*_ρ, N*_σ and obtains epimorphisms onto the outer group γ_{ρ,σ}. This is a step in describing the 'Teichmüller-type' symmetry group of a map/dessin (a quotient of the cartographic group) through stabilizers of the two elliptic generators.
errors: The claim 'Les homom i_ρ, i_σ aussi [injectifs], bien sûr' is not unconditional. As (39) itself states, it holds only when ρ^2 ≠ 1 (resp. σ^2 ≠ 1); presumably these are standing assumptions, matching the 'dès qu'on suppose ρ d'ordre 6' clauses.
'ρ^2≠1 ⇔ ρ≠-1' needs ρ≠1. This is implicit, since ρ = 1 would force the group to be generated by σ.

ideas.what: The amalgam GL(2,Z) = D_4 *_{D_2} D_6, with D_2 = {1,τ'}×{±1} the intersection of the dihedral stabilizers, mapped into the automorphism group of a quotient
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartographic groups and SL(2,Z)/GL(2,Z) but not this computation

ideas.what: Normalizer of a cyclic elliptic subgroup as the semidirect product of its centralizer with the reflection τ'; injectivity criterion τ'∉Z ⇔ ρ^2≠1

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-theoretic bookkeeping (centralizers, semidirect products, the D4*D2 D6 structure of GL(2,Z)) inside a longer unpublished computation of symmetry groups of maps. Nothing on this page is new beyond its context.
transcription_corrections: In (39), the final clause reads approximately '⇔ 𝔊^+ est isom. à un quotient de Z/4Z' (script G, not G). The mathematics confirms the reading: ρ^2 = 1 forces 𝔊^+ to be cyclic generated by σ.
(36) is a diamond-shaped diagram: {1,τ'}×{±1} maps to both D_ρ and D_σ, which map to N_ρ and N_σ, which in turn map to G_{ρ,σ} via i_ρ and i_σ. It is not two separate chains.
In the σ line of (39), something after 'σ^2≠1' is crossed out.
